entries.final_answer: The two seed init scenarios land bound and untagged, so they run in the gating 'not @wip and not @manual' nightly from day one (they are lightweight: each runs spec-kitty init in a temp repo and asserts). @manual is an allowed tag reserved for heavy or on-demand scenarios added later; core gives @manual, like @wip, no meaning beyond excluding the scenario from the gating nightly run. The bound-vs-@manual choice for future scenarios depends on their runtime cost.
options: Bound and untagged — run in the gating nightly from day one
Bound with inert @promise tags for QA to map later
Land as @wip — only the non-gating run executes them
entries.question: How should the two seed init scenarios be tagged, given core gives tags no meaning beyond the nightly 'not @wip and not @manual' filter and the promise index is out of core scope?

entries.final_answer: Generalize the shared guard: extend contracts/tools/gradle_pin_check.py so it also scans acceptance-jvm/ (build.gradle, pins.json, verification-metadata.xml) and the acceptance-bdd nightly job's gradle-version input, keeping one canonical pin-drift authority (GRADLE_PIN_MISMATCH). Update its unit tests under tests/contract/ accordingly. Fully satisfies NFR-003.
options: Generalize the shared gradle_pin_check.py to also scan acceptance-jvm
Give acceptance-jvm its own pin-check script
Accept unguarded pin-drift in v1, file a follow-up
entries.question: NFR-003 wants acceptance-jvm Gradle pin-drift guarded, but the shared guard contracts/tools/gradle_pin_check.py only scans contracts* paths. How should acceptance-jvm pins be guarded?
